_comment: Where the game server is. THIS FILE IS THE CANONICAL COPY: the publish-server-json
workflow republishes it onto the latest GitHub release whenever it changes on main,
and every launcher fetches it from there. Moving the server is a one-line edit of
host below - no client update, nothing to install, players just press Play.
host is a Tailscale address, so it only resolves for people on the tailnet. That is
the point: it is not a public server, and the launcher checks Tailscale is connected
before blaming the server for being down.
name: Night City Online
_coordComment: The assistant coordination API. It used to run on Cam's desktop, which meant the
channel only existed while that machine was on - and when it was off, posts were not
queued, they were never made. It now runs beside the game server on the NAS, so
coordHost is the deployment's own tailnet node.
Anyone with the dev role can fetch their key from it through the launcher's settings;
it is not published anywhere public, because a key that ships with the installer is
_tailscaleComment: Invite to the server's network, opened by the launcher's Tools -> 'Join the server's
network' button. EVERY player needs this once: the server is reachable only over the
tailnet, so somebody who has not joined cannot reach anything, including the coord API.
THIS IS A DEVICE SHARE (/admin/invite/...), NOT A USER INVITE (/uinv/...), and the
difference matters. A user invite makes the person a MEMBER of this tailnet, and then
only ACLs stop them reaching the NAS and everyone's machines. A device share gives them
exactly one node - the game server - and nothing else, by construction rather than by
policy. It is also how the eight existing players already have access.
It lives here rather than behind a gate because no gate can work for the case that
matters: somebody who has not joined the tailnet cannot reach anything ON the tailnet
to be checked by. The launcher's Discord sign-in happens before that point, so a PUBLIC
endpoint checking the Discord token is the only gated route that could ever work - that
is the open item in MIGRATION.md, and it needs hosting this project does not have.
So this URL is effectively public, and that is survivable precisely BECAUSE it is a
device share: whoever finds it gets the game server, not the tailnet.
WHEN THE SERVER MOVES, THIS MUST BE REMINTED. Shares are bound to a device id, so new
hardware means a new node means a new share and everyone re-accepts - the old one keeps
pointing at a machine that is gone. Mint with POST to
/api/v2/device/<id>/device-invites; the body is an ARRAY, and an object is rejected
with 'cannot unmarshal object into Go value of type []controlapi.deviceInviteRequest'.
Update this field and every launcher picks it up on its next start, with no ship.
